title: Computing new columns
summary: Vectorised arithmetic, assign, np.where, map with a dict, the .str accessor and pd.cut, without loops and without changing the input.
hints: `df.assign(total=...)` returns a **new** frame with the extra column and leaves `df` alone. Arithmetic on columns works element by element: `(df["quantity"] * df["unit_price"]).round(2)`. `add_size`: `np.where(df["quantity"] >= 10, "bulk", "single")` picks per row.

`add_region`: `df["country"].map(regions)` looks each value up in the dict; values that are not keys become `NaN`, so chain `.fillna("Other")`. `clean_products`: `df["product"].str.strip().str.title()`; each `.str` method applies a string method to every element.

`add_price_band`: `pd.cut(df["unit_price"], bins=[0, 5, 15, float("inf")], labels=["cheap", "mid", "premium"], right=False)`. `right=False` makes each bin include its left edge, so 5.0 is `"mid"`. Use `.assign(...)` for this one too (or `df.copy()` before assigning).
